ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a 4-to-1 multiplexer. The select inputs at the bottom are labeled S1 and S0, with S1 driven by A and S0 driven by B. The four data inputs on the left are labeled, from input 0 to input 3: C, ¬C, ¬C, C. The output on the right is labeled f. Reasoning: For a 4-to-1 MUX, select bits S1S0 choose input 0, 1, 2, or 3 respectively. Since S1=A and S0=B, AB=00 selects C, AB=01 selects ¬C, AB=10 selects ¬C, and AB=11 selects C. Thus f equals C when A and B are equal, and equals ¬C when A and B differ. Since A⊕B is 0 when A and B are equal and 1 when they differ, f = C⊕(A⊕B) = A⊕B⊕C.

method.method_draft: Read the MUX connections from the image: S1 is driven by A and S0 by B; the four inputs from top to bottom are C, \overline{C}, \overline{C}, C. Apply the MUX selection rule: AB=00 gives f=C, AB=01 gives f=\overline{C}, AB=10 gives f=\overline{C}, and AB=11 gives f=C. Thus f equals C when A and B are equal, and equals \overline{C} when A and B differ. Since A\oplus B is 0 when A and B are equal and 1 when they differ, f=C\oplus(A\oplus B)=A\oplus B\oplus C.
